facts.text: So it’s only natural that Trump’s new task force is named in accordance with this new branding.

The Wall Street Journal reports that Clayton will chair the Super Intelligence Force, effectively making him the new AI/SI czar, with Federal Trade Commission Chair Andrew Ferguson, Undersecretary of War for Research and Engineering Emil Michael, and Office of Personnel Management Director Scott Kupor serving as vice chairs.

Since then, Trump signed an executive order seeking to rebrand AI as “super intelligence,” a term seemingly embraced, with some stumbles , by the tech executives who gathered at the White House this week to sign a non-binding safety pledge. (The pledge included an impressive typo .)

Back in September, in response to an AI safety debate that the president has largely dismissed as a hoax created by “Radical Left Dumocrats,” Trump said he would nevertheless form an AI Force and appoint an AI czar (“Only High I.Q. individuals need apply!”).
Anthony Ha is TechCrunch’s weekend editor.
Previously, he worked as a tech reporter at Adweek, a senior editor at VentureBeat, a local government reporter at the Hollister Free Lance, and vice president of content at a VC firm.

He added that the SIF would, apart from Clayton, be led by Andrew Ferguson, chairman of the federal trade commission, Emil Michael, chief technology officer and under secretary of war for research and engineering, and Scott Kupor, director of the office of personnel management.ALSO READ:Trump's Ohio rally: How gas prices and AI data centres could shape November 2026 midterm electionsWhat Trump, AI CEOs agreed to in AI safety pact.

Venture capitalist David Sacks and former Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice will serve as external advisers.Sacks held the AI czar role at the start of Trump’s second term.TRUMP’S PUSH FOR ‘SUPER INTELLIGENCE’Trump described superintelligence as a technology that “many say is bigger than the Industrial Revolution, and the Internet”.He had announced the terminology change at the UN General Assembly, arguing that the word “artificial” made the technology sound fake.“The use of the word artificial intelligence makes it sound fake, and it is not fake.

Trump outlined the wide scope of outreach to "ensure that America continues to lead the World in Super Intelligence.""The Super Intelligence Force is tasked with coordinating the effort of the Federal Government to ensure that America continues to lead the World in Super Intelligence, which many say is bigger than the Industrial Revolution, and the Internet, and will protect the interests, and improve the lives, of all Americans," he wrote.Trump specified that the Super Intelligence Force will coordinate government engagement with "Federal Government's engagement with Consumers, Public Interest Groups, Religious Organizations, Critical Infrastructure Providers, and Super Intelligence Companies."The Super Intelligence Force will be led by a four-member leadership team spanning national intelligence, defence, regulatory, and federal personnel operations.

sources.title: Trump unveils his new Super Intelligence Force - TechCrunch
passages: So it’s only natural that Trump’s new task force is named in accordance with this new branding.

The Wall Street Journal reports that Clayton will chair the Super Intelligence Force, effectively making him the new AI/SI czar, with Federal Trade Commission Chair Andrew Ferguson, Undersecretary of War for Research and Engineering Emil Michael, and Office of Personnel Management Director Scott Kupor serving as vice chairs.

“The Super Intelligence Force is tasked with coordinating the effort of the Federal Government to ensure that America continues to lead the World in Super Intelligence, which many say is bigger than the Industrial Revolution, and the Internet, and will protect the interests, and improve the lives, of all Americans,” Trump said in a Sunday morning post on his social network Truth Social.

Since then, Trump signed an executive order seeking to rebrand AI as “super intelligence,” a term seemingly embraced, with some stumbles , by the tech executives who gathered at the White House this week to sign a non-binding safety pledge. (The pledge included an impressive typo .)

Back in September, in response to an AI safety debate that the president has largely dismissed as a hoax created by “Radical Left Dumocrats,” Trump said he would nevertheless form an AI Force and appoint an AI czar (“Only High I.Q. individuals need apply!”).
Anthony Ha is TechCrunch’s weekend editor.
Previously, he worked as a tech reporter at Adweek, a senior editor at VentureBeat, a local government reporter at the Hollister Free Lance, and vice president of content at a VC firm.

passages: He added that the SIF would, apart from Clayton, be led by Andrew Ferguson, chairman of the federal trade commission, Emil Michael, chief technology officer and under secretary of war for research and engineering, and Scott Kupor, director of the office of personnel management.ALSO READ:Trump's Ohio rally: How gas prices and AI data centres could shape November 2026 midterm electionsWhat Trump, AI CEOs agreed to in AI safety pact.

Why now?Trump, earlier this week, said tech executives agreed to establish voluntary standards for AI and reiterated his support for rapid expansion of data centers, Reuters news agency reported.The companies agreed to work with "independent auditors" to assess whether AI systems are working as their designers intended, according to a copy of the agreement posted by Trump on his social media platform.

sources.title: Bigger than industrial revolution: Trump announces Super Intelligence Force
passages: Venture capitalist David Sacks and former Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice will serve as external advisers.Sacks held the AI czar role at the start of Trump’s second term.TRUMP’S PUSH FOR ‘SUPER INTELLIGENCE’Trump described superintelligence as a technology that “many say is bigger than the Industrial Revolution, and the Internet”.He had announced the terminology change at the UN General Assembly, arguing that the word “artificial” made the technology sound fake.“The use of the word artificial intelligence makes it sound fake, and it is not fake.

Trump said it would work to maintain America’s global leadership in the frontier technology while protecting Americans’ interests.Trump announced the force on Truth Social following a White House accord in which leading technology companies pledged to uphold their responsibilities to the public.“The president asked that a group be put together,” Clayton said, adding that “the risk of not being first is high”.

Democratic and Republican lawmakers have called for greater government action.Trump has favoured limited regulation, arguing that excessive oversight could hamper growth and weaken US competitiveness against China.At an event in Washington on Tuesday, he said he did not want to work with Chinese President Xi Jinping on governing AI, arguing that doing so would make it harder for US companies to build better products than their Chinese rivals.“We’re leading now over China and everyone else, and I want to keep it that way,” Trump said.He also said he had discussed AI with Xi during the Chinese leader’s US visit the previous week, adding that Washington already works with Beijing “in so many ways”.- Ends

It will report to Trump and White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles.It will also coordinate federal engagement with consumers, public interest groups, religious organisations, critical infrastructure providers and companies developing superintelligence.Federal Trade Commission Chairman Andrew Ferguson, Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering Emil Michael and Office of Personnel Management Director Scott Kupor will serve as vice chairs.Members will include Vice President JD Vance, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Wiles.
